# Filter bar — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for the filter bar when the list needs facets: facet definitions turned into chips with saved views beside them. `filters` are filter-definition data — key, label, options, single or multi — so the whole bar is one declaration, and `savedViews` pins named filter sets like a bookings Today view beside the facets. Every toggle reports the merged active model through `onFiltersChange`, so the announcement and the state never disagree. There is no built-in filter modal or sheet: overflow UI stays host-owned behind `onOpenFilters`, and the bar reports the request rather than building the overlay. There is no URL sync inside either — the query adapters serialise the model, and wiring them to the address bar is the host's. The bar is a toolbar with an accessible name, facets group per definition, and saved views render as their own named group, so a saved view reads as a view rather than another filter.

## Native

### Features

Reach for the filter bar when the list needs facets: facet definitions turned into chips with saved views beside them — the native twin under the same contract. `filters` are filter-definition data — key, label, options, single or multi — so the whole bar is one declaration, and `savedViews` pins named filter sets like a bookings Today view beside the facets. Every toggle reports the merged active model through `onFiltersChange`, so the announcement and the state never disagree. There is no built-in filter sheet: overflow UI stays host-owned behind `onOpenFilters`, and the bar reports the request rather than building the overlay. There is no URL sync inside either — the query adapters serialise the model, and wiring them on is the host's. Facets group per definition with label and on-off state, and saved views render as their own named group.
